answer: Coordination Delay Ladder. Each agent identity must wait a fixed interval before its actions count toward any quorum, and the wait lengthens with the number of fresh identities joining in the same window. An attacker cannot forge simultaneous influence: flooding the mesa with new identities stretches their own activation timeline, so a coordinated push arrives too late. Honest agents pay little because they join gradually, like a steady zephyr rather than a gust.
